newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still mostly down late, May holds.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still mostly down late, May holds.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures remained mostly lower late Tuesday in moderate trade, but spot-May held relatively steady amid reports of stable to firmer physical prices, industry sources said.
At 1410 EDT, May inched up 0.4 cent to $2.068 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $2.035. June was 2.1 cents lower at $2.11. Most others also were down.

"We hit a point and there was some good buying down there, but I don't see it going up much from here. The weather's moderating," said one Texas-based trader, adding firmer physical prices could soften with milder temperatures.
With May Hub futures set to go off the board Thursday but cash only slightly over paper and spot open interest at manageable levels, most expected a relatively tame expiry.

Chart traders still pegged minor May support at $2.035, with further buying expected at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825. Key resistance was seen at $2.095, the intraday high from March 10, with a break above that level likely to trigger a test of the $2.16 area.

In June, resistance was seen first at $2.145, the 11 week high hit last week, then in the $2.21-2.23 gap from mid-January. June support was pegged at $2.085 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $1.98 area.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from a draw of 21 bcf to a build of 30 bcf versus a gain last year of 27 bcf.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly in the $2.04-2.09 area. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted in the mid-$2.30s, little changed on the day.
NYMEX said 22,298 Hub contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, May was still up by two cents at $1.95, while deferreds were unchanged to one cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.6 cents to 11.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT May natgas expires Friday, April 25.
